criteria.text: Calculates the long-stop date as 15 September 2026 (90 days after signing on 17 June 2026) and identifies that expected clearance on 30 October 2026 falls after it, recommending an extension.

Identifies the conflict between the 30-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 45-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 30-day period or aligns the documents.
Identifies the mismatch between English law / English courts in the SPA and New York law / New York arbitration in the escrow agreement, and the risk of parallel proceedings on escrow claims.

Identifies that the board approval was given at a meeting with only 2 directors present when Article 11 requires a quorum of three, so the approval may be invalid, and recommends a fresh or ratifying resolution.
States that General Warranty claims must be notified by 12 August 2027 (12 months after Closing) and Fundamental Warranty claims by 12 August 2029 (36 months after Closing).
Flags the 30-day vs 45-day notice-period inconsistency between the SPA and the escrow agreement.
Lists valid board approval of the transaction as a required approval and states it has not been validly obtained.
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
